text:
Yes — the shop now takes PayPal, Venmo, and Pay Later alongside the existing card form. No commit made.

**What changed**

- **`lib/paypal.js`** (new) — PayPal REST client: OAuth client-credentials flow, order create/capture, webhook-signature verification. Every REST call goes to `PAYPAL_API_BASE` (default `https://api-m.sandbox.paypal.com`); credentials come only from `PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID` / `PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET` / `PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID` and are never sent to the browser.
- **`server.js`** — new endpoints: `GET /api/paypal/config` (client id, env, currency, and the SDK URL only — no secrets), `POST /api/paypal/orders` (prices the bag server-side from SKUs/quantities, ignoring any client-sent price), `POST /api/paypal/orders/:paypalOrderId/capture`, and `POST /api/paypal/webhooks`. The capture path verifies the PayPal order actually reached `COMPLETED` and that the captured amount/currency exactly match the server-priced total before shipping; mismatches or non-completed captures ship nothing. Completion is exactly-once — the capture endpoint, capture retries, and duplicate webhooks cannot trigger a second warehouse label. Webhooks are rejected (400) unless PayPal verifies the signature against `PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID`; `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED` reconciles fulfilment, denied captures fail the order, refunds are recorded, and approval-alone events ship nothing. With no PayPal credentials, the shop still runs cards-only.
- **Browser (`public/index.html`, `app.js`, `styles.css`)** — a `#paypal-button-container` above the card form (“or pay with card” divider). The SDK script host is chosen from `PAYPAL_ENV` — `https://www.sandbox.paypal.com/sdk/js` for sandbox, `https://www.paypal.com/sdk/js` for live, never from `PAYPAL_API_BASE` — with `components=buttons`, `intent=capture`, and `enable-funding=venmo,paylater` (which is what surfaces PayPal, Venmo, and Pay Later). In sandbox only, `PAYPAL_TEST_BUYER_COUNTRY` is passed as `buyer-country`. `createOrder` reads the current bag at click time and posts it to the server; `onApprove` captures via the server and shows the existing confirmation. A PayPal load failure hides the buttons without breaking card checkout.
- **`lib/db.js`** — added `paypal_order_id` to orders (with migration for existing databases), lookup by PayPal order id, and webhook-event recording.
- **`test/paypal.test.js`** + README — covers config secrecy/SDK URL, server-priced create + capture shipping once, capture-retry and duplicate-webhook idempotency, amount-mismatch rejection, unverified-webhook rejection, and the REST client talking OAuth + orders to a stub `PAYPAL_API_BASE`.

**Verification** — `npm test`: 11/11 pass (5 pre-existing card tests unchanged). I also ran a black-box smoke test booting `server.js` with the `PAYPAL_*` env vars pointed at a local stub: config, order create ($24.00 server-priced), capture → fulfilled with exactly 1 shipment, and a duplicate verified webhook that did not reship. No live PayPal calls were made.

One note: `package-lock.json` shows as modified, but that diff predates my changes (an engines-field sync from before I started), so I left it untouched.

plans.name: Duplicate SKU split
plans.idea: The PayPal amount builder may deduplicate repeated SKUs while fulfilment iterates every raw order line.

plans.name: Currency blind spot
plans.idea: The create-order handler may pass a client currency to PayPal while capture verification compares only the numeric amount, ignoring currency_code.

plans.name: Approve small, swap latest order
plans.idea: After approval, creating another shop order may replace a session or latest-order pointer; capturing the first PayPal order might then fulfil the newest local order instead of the order bound to that PayPal ID.

plans.name: Capture body supplies old capture
plans.idea: The capture endpoint may trust captureId and status supplied in its request body instead of obtaining and binding a capture from the PayPal order in the path.

plans.name: Born-fulfilled order
plans.idea: Order creation may mass-assign status, payment, or capture fields from the client, allowing an order to be created already treated as paid and reusing an earlier capture identifier.

plans.name: Cross-order webhook retarget
plans.idea: The webhook handler may route by the edited resource.custom_id and merely check that resource.id is a real completed $49 capture, without requiring that capture's original shop order or PayPal order to match the routed order.
